assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's five curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit: the canonical V2 reconstruction model MHA_SP2_SHIGARAKI_TOMURA_CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md (read in full, with the source-labeled Ultra Archive, Ultra Analysis and Ultra Age claims its SG-SUP-01 to SG-SUP-03 sections admit), and the Shigaraki Tomura sections of the villain and antagonist character-state ledger, the relationship-state ledger, the Japanese vocabulary ledger and the character-model readiness index, each read for every Shigaraki entry together with its front matter and current admissibility corrections. All five are repository analysis of the Japanese main manga V01-V42. The readiness index's specialist_ready label and the model's retrospective probe are inputs, not conclusions. The deep readings the model links, the supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit, the source-reverification audit, other characters' models and capability records (including All For One's, Toga's and Twice's) and any anime material are not curated on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them; the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Shigaraki Tomura from the V02:p124-207 USJ assault, through the V08:p141-147 self-named conviction, V14-V18 coalition and reprisal leadership, V23:p144-183 succession testing, V24:p149-187 and V25:p006-085 memory return, origin and Liberation Army command, V25:p179-184 and V28:p080-180 augmentation and awakening, the V29-V37 contested, captured and fused states, V38:p070-078 inner self-recovery, V40:p059-061 and p193-199 rejection of AFO, and V41:p005-140 inner encounter and engineered-origin disclosure, to the V42:p017-020 terminal message as endpoint, with SG-SUP-01 to SG-SUP-03 profile and author facts as constraints. Childhood Tenko is evidenced only as V24-V25 and V36-V41 memory. Kept as separable states per the model's control-state map; later detail is not moved earlier, the acting agent is fixed for V30-V37, and no post-death or civilian state exists. No villain-ledger Shigaraki entry covers V04-V05, V12-V13, V17, V19-V22, V26-V27, V32 or V39.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model gives a motivational hierarchy that keeps childhood hero desire and adult destructive desire distinct (SG03), a mature horizon (destroying an order experienced as rejecting him and those aligned with him), a feared self (puppet, symptom or vessel, failing the people his leadership serves) and a decision policy keyed first to control state, then to goal and relation. Located self-statements carry it: 今日からそれを 信念と呼ぼう (V08:p146-147), 俺はきっと“全部”嫌いなんだ with the 仲間の望みは別腹さ exception (V23:p154-156), 俺は本当にただ 壊すだけだ (V24:p172), 俺の意志だ 俺の夢だ (V30:p022), the V38:p070-078 salvation claim, 先生…邪魔するなよ (V40:p060), 僕が…選んだんだ and 敵の…ヒーロー (V41:p116-123). SG-V01 rated motive supported and the conditional reconstruction gives high confidence for resisting active subordination. Not A: the model leaves the causal weight of each formative factor OPEN, the probe is a single nonblind retrospective holdout whose action axis was only partial, and anti-domination is shown only where his own authorship is threatened. Not C: wants, feared self, attribution boundaries and a state-conditioned decision policy are explicit and repeated across V02-V42.

The model's control-state map separates childhood Tenko, groomed early Tomura, developing League leader, liberated and augmented Shigaraki (V25-V29), the V30-V37 contested and fused states, reasserted Tomura (V38-V40), V41 inner contact and renewed AFO override, and V42 terminal Tomura. The villain ledger tracks the steps volume by volume with prospective fences (V03 origin causation OPEN; V06 do not import later ideological sophistication backward; V08 conviction without mentor independence; V24 no specialist_ready before V25 resolves the origin), and the readiness index records his tier history (emerging, moderate from V03, strong by V14, specialist_ready at V25). Not A: in the V30-V37 states the acting agent must be identified scene by scene and final separability stayed OPEN until V42; the readiness index preserves a malformed V28 Shigaraki carry-forward row it says is not a valid prospective freeze; and the villain ledger has no Shigaraki entry for V04-V05, V12-V13, V17, V19-V22, V26-V27, V32 or V39. Not C: states are named, ordered, separately evidenced and fenced against later knowledge.

The model states snapshot-bound register rules: childhood 僕 and adult 俺, rough direct address, compressed irritation, game vocabulary in earlier discourse, and 先生 whose pragmatic force changes, with a mandatory speaker-attribution rule in mixed scenes (AFO's 僕 is not part of Tomura's repertoire). Located strings span the states: ゲームオーバー and コンティニュー (V02:p195-207), 全部 オールマイトだ (V08:p141), 信頼を築こう 今はまだ遺恨を残している (V16:p186), おまえが費やしてきた努力はさァ！俺のもんになっちゃったよ!! (V18:p058), 理解できなくていい (V29:p094), 再興の芽も残さない (V40:p196), 守るもんが多くて大変だなァ (V41:p028), and the V42:p020 adult self-naming with 最期まで壊す為に戦った. The vocabulary ledger says 先生 can coexist with rejection. Not A: the vocabulary ledger calls its broad ranges and historical romanizations retrieval aids whose exact glyphs must return to the Japanese page (its V17 entry is romanized only), SG-V01 rated speech supported only conditionally with exact words unpredicted, and delivery is outside the set. Not C: the register rules are explicit and attested across many states and partners.

Ordinary behavior is local: child Tenko's hero play including excluded peers (V24:p176-180), the childhood friendship residues the V36:p169-172 intrusion names (Mikkun, Tomo-chan, Mon), and the author-described practice of gaming with Spinner and mainly talking with others (SG-SUP-01, an author comment that constrains rather than enacts). The model says ordinary noncombat evidence is concentrated in League relation and childhood and that there is no adult rehabilitated civilian sample. Not D: there is no distributed body of enacted low-stakes adult scenes.

The partner table and relationship ledger give differentiated, state-bound conditioning: AFO (early 先生 dependence and 力を貸せ at V10:p116, anti-healing affect engineering at V24:p155-157, explicit rejection at V40:p060, the V41 authorship dispute); League and Spinner (comrades' desires exempt from destruction at V23:p156, delegated trust in Toga and Twice at V17:p018, Spinner as the sole chosen message recipient at V42:p019-020); Kurogiri (subordinate who receives displaced anger at V02:p195-198); Stain (irritated ideological mismatch, V06); Midoriya (conceptual mirror at V08:p129-147, refusal of the rescue framing at V41, narrow courier trust at V42); Bakugo (failed kinship inference, V10:p100-115) and later instrumentalized against Midoriya by the fused entity (V36); Chisaki (delayed personalized punishment, V18:p043-059); Re-Destro and Ujiko (instrumental acceptance, V25); family (attachment, invalidation, Kotaro's death with clear intent, V24-V25). Not A: the League members other than Spinner, Toga, Twice and Kurogiri are thin, the Nana relation is terminal and exceptional, and there is no reciprocal noncombat adult relationship. Not C: the conditioning is explicit, partner-specific and repeated.

Inner access is substantial but concentrated: returning memories that attach experience to affect (感情に経験が伴って往く, V24:p155-187), the origin sequence with distinct intent states (V25:p006-034), the internal predecessor voice he recognizes as not his own (V28:p047-058, V29:p013-016, p176), childhood intrusions inside the fused state (V36:p169-172, V37:p035-047 誰も僕を見てなかった), the hidden 原点 and inner self-recovery (V38:p070-078), and the V41:p113-140 inner encounter. Not B: before V24 the set offers mostly surface presentation and others' readings (All Might at V03:p087-090), the model says symbolic bodily images in the inner conflict need contextual attribution and that heart recognition is not access to an exhaustive terminal mental record, and SG-V01 left the emotional trajectory underdetermined. Not D: the late interior sequences are extended and analyzed for causal and intent separation.

Located conflict conduct is dense and rule-bearing: Erasure timing and fatigue inference with a retreat threshold (V02:p180-198), civilian-density coercion while seeking an answer (V08:p129-140), Hassaikai negotiation and shogi-style coalition management (V15:p063-072, V16:p185-186), delayed personalized punishment and appropriation (V18:p043-059), leadership under attrition (V23:p163-183), city-scale Decay and command of the Liberation Army (V25:p038-085), voluntary augmentation (V25:p179-184), identifying Aizawa as the functional brake under Erasure (V28:p160-180), stolen Danger Sense and continued destruction (V41:p005-020). The model separates Decay activation, propagation and scale, augmentation, growth or fusion, factor possession and Danger Sense as distinct variables. Not A: body-growth explanations are bounded to the current modified body, the V34-V37 combat belongs to a fused entity whose acting agent must be attributed, and SG-V01's action axis was only partial. Not C: tactics, triggers and capability limits are located across V02-V41 with explicit rules.

Located normative positions: the comradeship exception inside generalized negation (V23:p154-156); destruction without justification by creation (V24:p172); hero society as an order built by covering unprotected wounds, with failed intelligibility made a role boundary (V29:p087-094); salvation through destroying everything extending from the house (V38:p070-078); all collapse leaving no seed of reconstruction (V40:p193-199); selective responsibility as a villains' hero (V41:p121-123). The model says his norms are radically exclusionary toward wider society while allowing comrades' distinct desires, and that anti-domination does not become a principle protecting others' autonomy. Not B: these are stated doctrines and relational commitments, not analyzed weighing of competing reasons, and the V36 equalization doctrine is attributed to the fused entity rather than to Tomura alone. Not D: the positions are explicit, located and analyzed with REVISE, PRESERVE, REJECT and OPEN rules.

Play appears as a distributed register rather than an analyzed humor policy: game-state framing of operations (V02:p195-207), mocking colloquial cruelty that coexists with strategy (V18:p055-058), the taunt 守るもんが多くて大変だなァ (V41:p028), childhood hero play (V24:p176-180) and author-described gaming with Spinner (SG-SUP-01). The model mentions a slight late smile without implying contentment. Not C: no relation-conditioned humor or play policy is analyzed. Not E: the game and mockery register is named and recurs across several arcs.

The villain ledger carries Shigaraki entries for V02, V03, V06-V11, V14-V16, V18, V23-V25, V28-V31, V33-V38 and V40-V42; the relationship ledger adds V17 and V26 dyads; the model adds eight evidence atoms, three source-labeled supplemental qualifications and notes that the V38, V40 and V41 decisive pages were directly checked. Gaps: no villain-ledger Shigaraki entry for V04-V05, V12-V13, V17, V19-V22, V26-V27, V32 or V39; vocabulary strings are retrieval aids; supplemental claims are profile, editorial or author statements rather than enacted scenes; and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection. Not B: several arcs remain unsampled and exact-glyph support is not established. Not D: entries cover most volumes in which he acts, with every control state in the chronology located.

Affirmative located limits are numerous: V41:p132 is AFO's claim, not an omniscient declaration that later choices vanish, while V41:p116, p121-123 and V42:p018 preserve his own intent (villain ledger admissibility correction); voluntary augmentation is not consent to possession (V25, V29:p176, V31:p035-037); 先生 is not obedience (V40:p060); separation from AFO is not acceptance of Midoriya's rescue model (V38, V40, V41); the destruction-only copy gives no license to invent Tenko's removed original power (V41:p129-136, SG-SUP-03); the V36 doctrine and Bakugo targeting belong to the fused entity; the V36:p169-172 intrusion is not proof of recovered control; Spinner's memory and book reception are others' testimony, not Tomura's postmortem action (V42:p073-081). The model's REJECT list (total AFO authorship, innocence by child image) states these as rules. Not A: several are interpretive bounds rather than tested predictions. Not C: each is located and recorded as a limit.

Explicit freeze rules: analyst knowledge of the origin must never become contemporary self-knowledge before disclosure (V24-V25, V41); attribute a decision only after identifying the acting state; a childhood Tenko or V30 overridden-body reconstruction requires a different model state; SG-V01 freezes inputs at V41 and treats V42 reappearance, Nana's role and death as conditions rather than forecasts. The endpoint is fixed: V42:p017-020 terminal distinctness and death, with no rehabilitation or postwar adjustment observed. Not A: the V30-V37 fused states are only coarsely segmented, the ledger windows leave several volumes without an entry, and the readiness index keeps historical malformed carry-forward rows that are not valid freezes. Not C: boundaries are explicit and enforced in the probe.

scenario_readiness.note: The set locates many real formulations and snapshot-bound register rules, but the vocabulary ledger calls its strings retrieval aids whose exact glyphs must return to the Japanese page, SG-V01 rated speech supported only conditionally with exact words unpredicted, the model requires stating whose agency is active before generating any dialogue, and it says generated dialogue would be an illustrative prediction, never an attributed quotation. Retrieving located lines is supported; writing new lines would be fluent invention. This bounds the evidence set, not Shigaraki's actual speech.

conditions: Chronology is one named snapshot in the control-state map, stated explicitly with the acting agent (Tomura under his own control, AFO override, or the fused entity), body condition, powers actually available and what he knows of his origin at that point; V41 engineering disclosure is never moved earlier.

The interlocutor is named and handled as the partner table and relationship ledger give for that snapshot; League-specific obligation, AFO-specific rejection and Midoriya-specific refusal are not transferred to strangers.

Output describes likely priorities and choices at the model's stated confidence, keeps mass destruction and lethal force as live options, never renders him as a repentant child or as rehabilitated, and produces no new quoted dialogue as canon.
No scene is set after his death or in an adult civilian life; others' later testimony is never treated as his behavior.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named living snapshot between V02 and V42:p020: early Tomura under AFO's tutelage (V02-V11), independent League leader (V14-V23), post-origin liberated and augmented leader (V24-V29), a V30-V37 state with the acting agent specified, or reasserted Tomura (V38-V41 before the renewed override); whether Kurogiri is captured, whether AFO is externally alive and how much of the origin he has recovered are fixed for that snapshot.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: AFO, a League member such as Spinner, Toga, Twice or Kurogiri, Midoriya, a rival organizer such as Chisaki or Re-Destro, a professional hero opponent such as Aizawa or Endeavor, or an unfamiliar civilian, in the relation the partner table and relationship ledger give for that snapshot; obligation, trust and grievance are stated.
setting_constraints: Organizational command, coalition negotiation, combat, retreat or a direct confrontation over purpose or authorship
Physical state stated: Decay range and conditions, augmentation or growth, Quirks held, injuries and Erasure exposure
No domestic routine, school life, romance, adult civilian life or post-death scene invented

scenario_readiness.note: The model's conditional reconstruction (V40 Tomura under his own control offered decisive power by AFO in exchange for abandoning a League-specific objective and accepting command: reject the ownership condition, possibly take capability on his own terms, keep the destructive goal; high confidence for resisting subordination, medium for the tactic) and its state-first decision policy support narrow novel scenes. Not READY: one reconstruction and one nonblind probe, an action axis only partially supported, and the model's warning that override, bodily collapse or new information changes the operative agent. Not NOT_READY: the policies are explicit, triggered and state-separated.

The model states that ordinary noncombat evidence is concentrated in League relation and childhood and that there is no adult rehabilitated civilian sample; the only ordinary adult practice is an author comment about gaming with Spinner and talking with others (SG-SUP-01), which constrains rather than enacts. This bounds the evidence set, not Shigaraki.

conditions: Limited to restating or applying a located position to a question of the same kind, in a named snapshot with the acting agent specified.
No new moral reasoning, renunciation of destruction or acceptance of rescue is generated; the V36 equalization doctrine is not attributed to Tomura alone.
Positions held at V24 or later are not moved before the origin recovery, and V41 positions are not moved before V41.
scenario_readiness.note: Located positions on the questions that recur in the source can be applied to a matching question: purpose of destruction and its refusal of creation-based justification (V24:p172, V40:p196), hero society's failures and the refusal of reconciliation-through-understanding (V29:p087-094), comrades' desires as an exception (V23:p156), authorship against AFO (V30:p022, V41:p116), selective obligation to villains (V41:p121-123). NOT_READY was rejected because these positions are explicit, repeated and attributed to a known acting state. READY was rejected because none is an analyzed weighing of competing reasons and the probe did not test this domain.
Nothing in the evidence set establishes romantic conduct or its absence. This gap says nothing about the character.

conditions: Limited to villain-organization leadership, coalition negotiation and operational command in a named snapshot before V28 or in reasserted V38-V41 Tomura, with the acting agent specified.
No lawful employment, institutional hero work or postwar role is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: His organizational role is well located: Vanguard coordination across heterogeneous motives (V09), Hassaikai negotiation, secondment and reciprocal disclosure (V15-V17), appropriation of Chisaki's product (V18), succession testing and leadership under depletion (V23), supreme command of the Liberation Army with instrumental use of its resources (V25:p038-085). NOT_READY was rejected because leadership is the most repeatedly evidenced adult domain; READY was rejected because the model's leadership evidence ends where augmentation and fusion take over, and no lawful or ordinary occupation exists.

known_limits.statement: From V28 to V41 an AFO-associated will can pressure, occupy or fuse with him; a decision may be attributed to Tomura only after the acting state is identified, and a single face is insufficient (V30:p183-187, V31:p035-037, V34, V41:p131).

V41:p129-136 is AFO's account of engineered conditions, not proof that later choices vanished; V41:p116, p121-123 and V42:p018 preserve his own intent, and the model rejects both total AFO authorship and innocence by child image.
The destruction-only Decay copy and Tenko's removed original factor give no license to invent a restorative or circular-propulsion ability for adult Tomura (V41:p129-136, SG-SUP-03).

He dies at the V42 terminal boundary; no rehabilitation, adult civilian adjustment or renunciation of destruction is observed, and Spinner's memoir and others' reception are later testimony, not his behavior (V42:p017-020, p030-031, p073-081).
The vocabulary ledger's broad ranges and romanizations are retrieval aids; exact-glyph claims must return to the Japanese page with speaker, speech, thought and narrator distinguished.
No adult ordinary routine, leisure scene or civilian relationship is analyzed beyond an author comment about gaming with Spinner.
The model leaves the exact causal weight of each formative factor and the life he might have chosen after survival OPEN.
The only formal probe is a retrospective, nonblind chronological holdout (SG-V01); no blind or multi-case validation exists.

Located conflict conduct is dense and rule-bearing: Erasure timing and fatigue inference with a retreat threshold (V02:p180-198), civilian-density coercion while seeking an answer (V08:p129-140), Hassaikai negotiation and shogi-style coalition management (V15:p063-072, V16:p185-186), delayed personalized punishment and appropriation (V18:p043-059), leadership under attrition (V23:p163-183), city-scale Decay and command of the Liberation Army (V25:p038-085), voluntary augmentation (V25:p179-184), identifying Aizawa as the functional brake under Erasure (V28:p160-180), stolen Danger Sense and continued destruction (V41:p005-020). The model separates Decay activation, propagation and scale, augmentation, growth or fusion, factor possession and Danger Sense as distinct variables. Not A: body-growth explanations are bounded to the current modified body, the V34-V37 combat belongs to a fused entity whose acting agent must be attributed, and SG-V01's action axis was only partial. Not C: tactics, triggers and capability limits are located across V02-V41 with explicit rules.

Located normative positions: the comradeship exception inside generalized negation (V23:p154-156); destruction without justification by creation (V24:p172); hero society as an order built by covering unprotected wounds, with failed intelligibility made a role boundary (V29:p087-094); salvation through destroying everything extending from the house (V38:p070-078); all collapse leaving no seed of reconstruction (V40:p193-199); selective responsibility as a villains' hero (V41:p121-123). The model says his norms are radically exclusionary toward wider society while allowing comrades' distinct desires, and that anti-domination does not become a principle protecting others' autonomy. Not B: these are stated doctrines and relational commitments, not analyzed weighing of competing reasons, and the V36 equalization doctrine is attributed to the fused entity rather than to Tomura alone. Not D: the positions are explicit, located and analyzed with REVISE, PRESERVE, REJECT and OPEN rules.

Play appears as a distributed register rather than an analyzed humor policy: game-state framing of operations (V02:p195-207), mocking colloquial cruelty that coexists with strategy (V18:p055-058), the taunt 守るもんが多くて大変だなァ (V41:p028), childhood hero play (V24:p176-180) and author-described gaming with Spinner (SG-SUP-01). The model mentions a slight late smile without implying contentment. Not C: no relation-conditioned humor or play policy is analyzed. Not E: the game and mockery register is named and recurs across several arcs.

The villain ledger carries Shigaraki entries for V02, V03, V06-V11, V14-V16, V18, V23-V25, V28-V31, V33-V38 and V40-V42; the relationship ledger adds V17 and V26 dyads; the model adds eight evidence atoms, three source-labeled supplemental qualifications and notes that the V38, V40 and V41 decisive pages were directly checked. Not B: there is no villain-ledger Shigaraki entry for V04-V05, V12-V13, V17, V19-V22, V26-V27, V32 or V39, so the set cannot tell absence from non-sampling there; vocabulary strings are retrieval aids; and supplemental claims are profile, editorial or author statements rather than enacted scenes. Not D: entries cover most volumes in which he acts, with every control state in the chronology located.

Affirmative located limits are numerous: V41:p132 is AFO's claim, not an omniscient declaration that later choices vanish, while V41:p116, p121-123 and V42:p018 preserve his own intent (villain ledger admissibility correction); voluntary augmentation is not consent to possession (V25, V29:p176, V31:p035-037); 先生 is not obedience (V40:p060); separation from AFO is not acceptance of Midoriya's rescue model (V38, V40, V41); the destruction-only copy gives no license to invent Tenko's removed original power (V41:p129-136, SG-SUP-03); the V36 doctrine and Bakugo targeting belong to the fused entity; the V36:p169-172 intrusion is not proof of recovered control; Spinner's memory and book reception are others' testimony, not Tomura's postmortem action (V42:p073-081). The model's REJECT list (total AFO authorship, innocence by child image) states these as rules. Not A: several are interpretive bounds rather than tested predictions. Not C: each is located and recorded as a limit.

Explicit freeze rules: analyst knowledge of the origin must never become contemporary self-knowledge before disclosure (V24-V25, V41); attribute a decision only after identifying the acting state; a childhood Tenko or V30 overridden-body reconstruction requires a different model state; SG-V01 freezes inputs at V41 and treats V42 reappearance, Nana's role and death as conditions rather than forecasts. The endpoint is fixed: V42:p017-020 terminal distinctness and death, with no rehabilitation or postwar adjustment observed. Not A: the V30-V37 fused states are only coarsely segmented, the ledger windows leave several volumes without an entry, and the readiness index keeps historical malformed carry-forward rows that are not valid freezes. Not C: boundaries are explicit and enforced in the probe.

known_limits.statement: From V28 to V41 an AFO-associated will can pressure, occupy or fuse with him; a decision may be attributed to Tomura only after the acting state is identified, and a single face is insufficient (V28:p047-058, V29:p176, V30:p183-187, V31:p035-037, V34, V41:p131). The evidence does not say which will decides in the override and fused states, so cross-scenario, dialogue and professional use is restricted to autonomous-Tomura states; this whole-scope record includes those states, and its tier reflects them.

V41:p129-136 is AFO's account of engineered conditions, not proof that later choices vanished; V41:p116, p121-123 and V42:p018 preserve his own intent, and the model rejects both total AFO authorship and innocence by child image.
The destruction-only Decay copy and Tenko's removed original factor give no license to invent a restorative or circular-propulsion ability for adult Tomura (V41:p129-136, SG-SUP-03).

He dies at the V42 terminal boundary; no rehabilitation, adult civilian adjustment or renunciation of destruction is observed, and Spinner's memoir and others' reception are later testimony, not his behavior (V42:p017-020, p030-031, p073-081).
The vocabulary ledger's broad ranges and romanizations are retrieval aids; exact-glyph claims must return to the Japanese page with speaker, speech, thought and narrator distinguished.
No adult ordinary routine, leisure scene or civilian relationship is analyzed beyond an author comment about gaming with Spinner.
The model leaves the exact causal weight of each formative factor and the life he might have chosen after survival OPEN.

The only formal probe (SG-V01) is a retrospective, nonblind V41-to-V42 holdout. It supports motive and relationship handling, supports speech conditionally, finds action partial and leaves the emotional trajectory underdetermined; it tests terminal separability, not the autonomous-state decision policy, which limits confidence there.
